extra_events.title: Senior Weightroom Orientation Series Begins
extra_events.body: Senior Weightroom Orientation Series Begins Tuesday, September 15, 2026 Build confidence and learn the essentials in this supportive six-week strength series for senior adults. Designed for those new to weight training, participants will learn proper machine setup, safe lifting technique, and how to track progress in a welcoming, small-group environment. Each week builds on foundational movement patterns, posture, and gradual progression under the guidance of a Certified Personal Trainer. Leave feeling comfortable, capable, and ready to use the fitness center independently.

extra_events.title: Watercolor Painting Class
extra_events.body: Watercolor Painting Class Tuesday, October 20, 2026 Curious about watercolor but not sure where to begin? This relaxed, beginner-friendly workshop is the perfect introduction to painting with watercolors. Kristi will guide you step-by-step through the entire process as you create a spring flowers painting, making it approachable and fun, even if you’ve never painted before. This is a fully instructor-led class designed for beginners. All watercolor materials are provided, so you can simply show up ready to learn, experiment, and enjoy the creative process. By the end of class, you’ll leave with a finished painting and a better understanding of how watercolor works.

extra_events.title: Splashing Pumpkins
extra_events.body: Splashing Pumpkins Looking for something different this spooky season? Come make a splash at our 4th annual floating pumpkin patch! From 1:30 to 4:15 PM, you can dive in and take home a pumpkin of your choice for only $8! All are welcome! Families, couples, singles and the young at heart. Capacity is limited to 45 pumpkin pickers at a time, register below for a time block to avoid disappointment! Chaperones must be 16 years of age or older and are welcome to get in the water. Please remember that non swimmers and children aged 6 and under must be within arms reach at all times! THE HOT TUB AND POOL WILL BE CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC. Sauna and steam room will remain open. extra_events.title: Día de los Muertos Exhibit - Arcos y Portales
extra_events.body: Día de los Muertos Exhibit - Arcos y Portales Thursday, September 24, 2026 Join the City of Lafayette Arts and Cultural Resources Department at The Collective Community Arts Center for the Annual Día de los Muertos Exhibit. Look forward to local art by Arlette Lucero, Jesus Sales, Michelle Sepulveda, Lida Penkova, Justice High School Students, and Centaurus High School Students, and more representing and celebrating this Mexican tradition. Add to the community ofrendas honoring our ancestors and those we have lost. Lafayetteco.gov/Collective Join us: Friday, Oct. 9, 4:30-6:30pm - Paper Catrina Workshop. Join local crafter Martha Ramírez to make a paper Día de los Muertos elegant woman called a Catrina. Cut, fold, and glue simple materials to create a standing Catrina to take with you and help welcome your ancestors home for Día de los Muertos. Martha will instruct step by step. This workshop will be predominantly presented in Spanish. Request language interpretation by email at arts@lafayetteco.gov . Saturday and Sunday, Oct. 24 and 25 - Picture Frame Decorating Drop In. Decorate and take home a picture frame to begin your own ofrenda at home. Add a picture of a loved one who has passed. While supplies last. Friday, Oct. 30, 3-7pm - Exhibit Closing Celebration. Lets welcome our ancestors home with facepainting, music, and community. Light mexican food and refreshments provided. 3-5pm - Facepainting 5-7pm - Music and Light Appetizers Visit The Collective Community Arts Center at 201 N Public Road in Lafayette and find more details at lafayetteco.gov/Collective

extra_events.body: Art on the Street, See & Respond 2026 See & Respond Exhibition The See & Respond exhibit is on display at the Lafayette Public Library on the main floor, Oct. 2 - Nov. 1. extra_events.title: Lafayette Cultural Arts Board Meeting
extra_events.body: Lafayette Cultural Arts Board (LCAB) promotes, nurtures, and celebrates the visual, performing, and language arts by providing opportunities for the public to appreciate and enjoy art in its various forms; connecting artists, educators, and community members with resources; building partnerships to sustain and further the arts; and embracing and supporting the diversity of the community we serve. LCAB works closely with the Arts and Cultural Resources Department to plan and implement programs for the community.

extra_events.body: Community Police Academy meets once a week for 10 weeks and each block provides participants first-had information by officers and includes hands-on and interactive opportunities.
